passage:
For the third time that evening, Saurabh took the phone from his father Farhan and opened the payment app. "See, Papa, first the green button, then the number."
Farhan squinted. "Which green?"
Saurabh felt a sigh rising and swallowed it. He remembered Papa at the school gate, showing him how to tie his shoelaces again and again without once saying, "How many times?"
"Here," he said gently, and tapped more slowly. "You press, I'll watch."
Farhan pressed the wrong one and laughed. "Again?"
"Again," said Saurabh.
On the fifth try it worked, and Farhan held the phone up like a trophy.

qa.q: What did Saurabh swallow when Farhan asked 'Which green?'
qa.a: A sigh.

qa.q: What is Saurabh feeling when Farhan asks the question again?
qa.a: Frustrated and tempted to sigh, but he steadies himself by remembering how patiently his father taught him.

qa.q: What choice helped Saurabh keep his tone steady?
qa.a: He remembered Papa teaching him to tie his shoelaces again and again, then slowed down and let Farhan press while he watched.

qa.q: How might Farhan feel when the phone finally works?
qa.a: Proud and pleased, holding the phone up like a trophy after laughing off the earlier mistake.

grounding: A young adult keeps a steady tone while explaining an app to a parent for the third time.

Anjali: Papa, tap the camera icon. The one that looks like a little movie camera.
Nilesh: This one?
Anjali: Yes. Now Ruhi's name.
Nilesh: Nothing's happening.
Anjali: It's loading. Wait one second.
Nilesh: I can't see her. Is it broken?
Anjali: No, it's just slow. See the circle spinning? That means it's trying.
Nilesh: Third time you're telling me this. Sorry, beta.
Anjali: It's okay. You told me how to read the clock about a hundred times. You held my hand.
Nilesh: Did I?
Anjali: Every evening, Papa. Now tap.
Nilesh: Ah! It's ringing! Hello, Ruhi! Look, Anju, I did it!
Anjali: You did.

qa.q: What does the camera icon look like?
qa.a: A little movie camera.

qa.q: What is Anjali feeling when Nilesh says sorry for asking a third time?
qa.a: Warm and reassuring. Anjali tells Nilesh it is okay and reminds Nilesh how patiently he taught Anjali the clock.

qa.q: What could Anjali do next time Nilesh struggles with the app?
qa.a: Anjali could repeat the steps slowly and let Nilesh tap himself, as Anjali does, or write the steps on a card for Nilesh to keep.

qa.q: How might Nilesh feel when the call rings and Ruhi answers?
qa.a: Delighted and relieved, since he greets Ruhi happily after the struggle.

grounding: A young adult keeps a steady tone teaching a parent an app, returning the patience once received.

passage:
Last Sunday my mother, Bidisha, asked me for the third time that week how to send a photo on the chat app. I felt the old irritation rise; I was in the middle of my own work. I nearly said, "Ma, I've shown you twice!"
Then I remembered her at the kitchen table when I was seven, going over the same long division with me every evening for a month without once raising her voice.
So I sat down next to her and took my hands off the phone. "You do it, I'll watch." She pressed the wrong button, laughed, tried again. Paperclip, gallery, photo, send. On the fourth try it went. Her face lit up like a child's.
I'm Pallavi, and I've decided the third time is just part of the deal.

qa.q: What were the steps to send the photo?
qa.a: Paperclip, gallery, photo, send.

qa.q: What did Pallavi feel when asked for the third time?
qa.a: Pallavi felt irritation rise, being in the middle of work.

qa.q: What did Pallavi do that made the lesson work?
qa.a: Pallavi took hands off the phone and let Bidisha press the buttons herself, keeping a steady tone through the mistakes.

qa.q: How did Bidisha feel when the photo finally went?
qa.a: Bidisha felt delighted, her face lighting up like a child's.

grounding: Shows a young adult keeping a steady tone while explaining an app to a parent for the third time, returning patience once received.

passage:
Care home staff note, Saturday visit.
Mrs Ganga Iyer's granddaughter, Seema, spent an hour today teaching her video calls on the new tablet. I watched from the desk. Mrs Iyer forgot which button to press three times and apologised each time. Seema said "No problem, Paati" every single time, in the same easy voice. No sighing. She wrote the steps in big letters on a card and stuck it to the tablet cover.
At the end Mrs Iyer made a test call to Seema's phone across the room. They both waved and laughed as if it were a great joke.
Next step: use Seema's card to help Mrs Iyer call her son on Wednesday.

qa.q: Where did Seema stick the steps?
qa.a: On a card stuck to the tablet cover.

qa.q: How did Mrs Ganga Iyer feel each time she forgot?
qa.a: Mrs Iyer felt embarrassed and sorry, apologising each time.

qa.q: What did Seema do that showed patience?
qa.a: She kept the same easy voice through three mistakes and wrote the steps in big letters on a card.

qa.q: How does the note-writer plan to build on Seema's visit?
qa.a: The note-writer will use Seema's card to help Mrs Iyer call her son on Wednesday.

grounding: Shows a young adult teaching an elder a device with a steady, respectful tone despite repeated forgetting.

passage:
Thursday night
Taught Dad the bank app again. Third time this month. He wrote everything in his little notebook last time and still got lost at the password screen.
I felt myself getting sharp. Then I noticed his hand shaking a little on the phone, and how he kept saying, "Sorry, son, I'm slow now." This is Kiran, the man the whole building used to call to fix every fuse and tap.
So I slowed down. One step, then wait. I let him type. When he got it wrong, I said, "That's fine, that screen confuses everyone." It took forty minutes. At the end he checked his balance himself and grinned.
He said, "Thank you for not making me feel old." That's the line I'm writing down.
Thomas

qa.q: How long did the lesson take?
qa.a: Forty minutes.

qa.q: What made Thomas slow down?
qa.a: Thomas felt tenderness and respect on noticing Kiran's shaking hand and apology, remembering him as the man who fixed everything.

qa.q: What did Thomas do that made the lesson go well?
qa.a: He went one step at a time, let Kiran type, and reassured him that the screen confuses everyone.

qa.q: How did Kiran feel at the end?
qa.a: Kiran felt grateful and pleased, grinning and thanking Thomas for not making him feel old.

grounding: Shows a young adult staying patient while teaching a parent an app for the third time, as a form of respect.

Baljeet: Kunal, the photo is not going again. I pressed the pin.
Kunal: No problem, Papa. The pin is for files. Do you see the small camera next to it?
Baljeet: I saw camera. It opened my own face 😅
Kunal: That's the front camera. Tap the two round arrows at the bottom, then it will show the garden.
Baljeet: Sorry beta, third time I am asking this week.
Kunal: Ask thirty times. You taught me to tie my shoelaces for one whole summer 🙂
Baljeet: That was different, you were small.
Kunal: And now you're new at this. Try once more, I'm right here.
(Four minutes later a slightly blurry photo of the tulsi plant arrives in the family group.)
Baljeet: Sent!! 👍
Kunal: Perfect. Mummy will love it.

qa.q: What happened when Baljeet tapped the camera?
qa.a: It opened Baljeet's own face, because it was the front camera.

qa.q: What does Kunal's message about the shoelaces suggest about how he feels toward Baljeet?
qa.a: It suggests Kunal feels grateful and fond, remembering Baljeet's patience with him as a child, so helping now feels like giving that back.

qa.q: Which of Kunal's replies helped most, and why?
qa.a: "Ask thirty times" took away Baljeet's embarrassment, and giving one small step at a time made the task feel doable.

qa.q: What is it like for Baljeet when Kunal keeps a steady tone?
qa.a: Baljeet can keep trying without feeling foolish, and his "Sent!!" shows how pleased he is to manage it himself.

grounding: Shows a young adult calmly explaining a phone app to a parent for the third time, linking patience to what the parent once gave.
